text:
Nina Patel: bringing bronte9b-int4 into our canary ring today. quick smoke found OOMs correlated with bursts where clients request long generations (>200 tokens).
Rahul Desai: thanks. which params reproduced it?
Nina Patel: simple repro: ```
curl -X POST https://canary.api/v1/generate -d '{"model":"bronte9b-int4","inputs":"Explain the plot of ...","max_new_tokens":300,"batch_size":6}'
```
Lena Park: saw that pattern last week on another model. charts showed lots of small free slabs but no single chunk big enough for a 48MB allocation -> fragmentation.
Rahul Desai: three quick knobs to try: lower max_new_tokens default to 128, reduce microbatch to 3, and disable kv_prefetch for this canary. tradeoffs?
Nina Patel: ran a short sweep: batch=3 + max_new_tokens=128 + kv_prefetch=false -> OOMs from 22->1 over 6h. latency p95 up ~30ms. throughput -12%.
ops-bot: canary-deploy bronte9b-int4 config=frag-mit-v1 by nina-patel deployed on 4/8 hosts :white_check_mark:
Rahul Desai: that looks safe. propose staged rollout: 15% immediate, monitor 1h for OOMs and slab_fragmentation_ratio, then 50% if ok, full after 12h.
Lena Park: add per-host alert: slab_fragmentation_ratio > 0.6 for 5m and free_contig_max < 16MB for 2m. also log host histograms to the ticket.
Nina Patel: creating ticket RI-5772 with perf graphs, log excerpts, and canary diffs. will include a tiny reproducer in scripts/onboard/bronte_smoke.sh.
Rahul Desai: small FYI — runtime already supports an on-request compaction flag, but we haven't tested it live. maybe enable it in next experiment rather than now.
Lena Park: agree. also let's add a follow-up RFC to consider adaptive compaction: trigger compaction when fragmentation ratio exceeds threshold and recent allocation failures > 0.
Nina Patel: will do. tagging @infra for kernel slab metrics access on RI-5772. I'll post the PR link once ready.
Rahul Desai: thanks, please ping in #release-war-room before staging the 50% step.
Nina Patel: will do. :thumbsup:
